back: The purpose for which land is used: cultivation, grazing, forestry, mining, settlement, transport, recreation, conservation.

front: Explaining land use from a map
back: Identify, locate (grid reference), then explain with map evidence: contours, water, routes, symbols.
Nucleated (grouped), dispersed (scattered homesteads), linear (along a road, river or railway).
Many services → service/administrative centre; shafts and dumps → mining; sidings and junctions → transport; lodges → tourism.
Dendritic: tree-like, acute-angled junctions, uniform rock. Trellis: parallel streams, right-angled tributaries, alternating hard and soft rock.
Radial: outward from a central dome or cone. Parallel: side by side down a uniform slope.
Routes follow valleys, cross ridges at cols, bridge rivers at narrow points and avoid steep or marshy land.
Point: position only (borehole). Line: length (road, river). Area/polygon: covers space (forest, dam).
